answer: jsonschema is imported at runtime by tools/plugin/payload.py, tools/plugin/exec_policy.py, tools/marketplace/handoff.py and tools/marketplace/manifest_reader.py. There is no pyproject.toml / setup.py / requirements.txt, and the packed plugin artifact does not vendor jsonschema. Hiding jsonschema makes exec_policy.validate_policy raise. Three golden journeys against the installed packed payload still pass because they are stdlib-only. SUCCESS:TST-0070

evidence.claim: The published tar.gz is unpacked to a scratch payload and installed into an empty profile. plugin.json at the dest exists, parses, and meets MIN_BYTES. The unpack path is not tools/plugin.
Three golden journeys run against the INSTALLED tree and each produce a JSON file that exists, parses, and is >=256 bytes. Truncating one file makes the postcondition fail.
jsonschema is a runtime import in plugin/marketplace and is load-bearing for exec_policy.validate_policy. It is absent from the packed artifact and from packaging metadata.
